source: Technology Promotion Project to Increase Productivity Around Tonle Sap (TSTD — TA 7305-CAM), watermelon (ដំណាំឪឡឹក) technical training booklet, prepared by the project's agricultural techniques and extension officer in cooperation with East West Seed International, November 2016. Contact: livleanghy@gmail.com
text:
Seedlings in the nursery should be watered regularly, roughly every 2 to 3 days, to keep the growing medium moist. Watermelon seedlings are generally ready to be transplanted into the field at about 8 to 10 days after sowing/germination.

Before transplanting, harden off the seedlings by reducing watering and gradually exposing them to more sun for about a week beforehand, so they adjust to outdoor field conditions.

Planting holes in the mulched/prepared bed should be pre-watered a few days (roughly 3 to 5 days) before transplanting so the soil in the hole is adequately moist for the seedling roots.

Transplant the young seedling into the planting hole, keeping the root ball's soil level even with the surrounding bed surface, then gently press soil around the base of the stem to firm it in place.
